title: Lesson Timetable
statementMd:
When Petya has free from computer games time, he attends university classes. Every day the lessons on Petya’s faculty consist of two double classes. The floor where the lessons take place is a long corridor with $*M*$ classrooms numbered from $1$ to $*M*$, situated along it.

All the students of Petya’s year are divided into $*N*$ groups. Petya has noticed recently that these groups’ timetable has the following peculiarity: the number of the classroom where the first lesson of a group takes place does not exceed the number of the classroom where the second lesson of this group takes place.

Once Petya decided to count the number of ways in which one can make a lesson timetable for all these groups. The timetable is a set of $2*N*$ numbers: for each group the number of the rooms where the first and the second lessons take place. Unfortunately, he quickly lost the track of his calculations and decided to count only the timetables that satisfy the following conditions:

1) On the first lesson in classroom $*i*$ exactly $*X*_{*i*}$ groups must be present.

2) In classroom $*i*$ no more than $*Y*_{*i*}$ groups may be placed.

Help Petya count the number of timetables satisfying all those conditionsю As there can be a lot of such timetables, output modulo $10^{9} + 7$.

## Input

The first line contains one integer $*M*$ ($1 ≤ *M* ≤ 100$) — the number of classrooms.

The second line contains $*M*$ space-separated integers — $*X*_{*i*}$ ($0 ≤ *X*_{*i*} ≤ 100$) the amount of groups present in classroom $*i*$ during the first lesson.

The third line contains $*M*$ space-separated integers — $*Y*_{*i*}$ ($0 ≤ *Y*_{*i*} ≤ 100$) the maximal amount of groups that can be present in classroom $*i*$ at the same time.

It is guaranteed that all the $*X*_{*i*} ≤ *Y*_{*i*}$, and that the sum of all the $*X*_{*i*}$ is positive and does not exceed $1000$.

## Output

In the single line output the answer to the problem modulo $10^{9} + 7$.

## Note

In the second sample test the first and the second lessons of each group must take place in the same classroom, that’s why the timetables will only be different in the rearrangement of the classrooms’ numbers for each group, e.g. $3! = 6$.
statementZhMd:
当 Petya 不玩电脑游戏时，他会去上大学课程。Petya 所在系每天的课程由两节连堂课组成。上课的楼层是一条长走廊，沿走廊有 $*M*$ 间教室，编号为 $1$ 到 $*M*$。

Petya 所在年级的学生被分成了 $*N*$ 个小组。最近，Petya 注意到这些小组的课程表有一个特点：每个小组第一节课所在教室的编号不大于第二节课所在教室的编号。

有一天，Petya 决定统计所有小组课程表的可能数量。课程表由 $2*N*$ 个数构成：对每个小组，记录其第一节课和第二节课所在教室的编号。遗憾的是，他很快就算乱了，于是决定只统计满足以下条件的课程表：

1) 第一节课时，教室 $*i*$ 中恰好有 $*X*_{*i*}$ 个小组上课。

2) 教室 $*i*$ 中同时上课的小组数不超过 $*Y*_{*i*}$。

请帮助 Petya 统计满足所有条件的课程表数量。由于答案可能很大，请对 $10^{9} + 7$ 取模后输出。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*M*$（$1 ≤ *M* ≤ 100$），表示教室数量。

第二行包含 $*M*$ 个以空格分隔的整数 $*X*_{*i*}$（$0 ≤ *X*_{*i*} ≤ 100$），表示第一节课时在教室 $*i*$ 上课的小组数。

第三行包含 $*M*$ 个以空格分隔的整数 $*Y*_{*i*}$（$0 ≤ *Y*_{*i*} ≤ 100$），表示同一时间可在教室 $*i*$ 上课的小组数上限。

保证对于所有 $i$，均有 $*X*_{*i*} ≤ *Y*_{*i*}$，且所有 $*X*_{*i*}$ 之和为正数且不超过 $1000$。

## 输出格式

单行输出问题的答案对 $10^{9} + 7$ 取模后的结果。

## 说明

在第二个样例中，每个小组的第一节课和第二节课都必须在同一间教室上，因此不同的课程表只在各组对应的教室编号排列上有所区别，例如 $3! = 6$。
